home.title: Who decides how internet names and numbers work, and how you can have a say.
home.lede: ICANN is not one organization but a set of groups with different jobs. This guide maps them, explains each in plain language, and points you to the official places to take part.
home.partsLede: Most confusion about ICANN goes away once you separate who proposes, who decides, and who carries it out.
home.part.communityText: Supporting Organizations develop policy. Advisory Committees give advice. Both are made up of volunteers from registries, registrars, governments, businesses, civil society and individual users.
home.part.boardText: Sixteen voting Directors take the final decision on policy recommendations and must consider the advice they receive.
home.part.orgText: The staff, led by the President and CEO, put the Board's decisions into practice and support the community's work.
familyDesc.policy: Runs a formal process and sends recommendations to the Board
familyDesc.advice: Gives advice the Board must consider. Not a reporting line
familyDesc.accountability: Answers to, or can hold to account
familyDesc.implementation: Carries out decisions or operates functions
familyDesc.selection: Picks voting members or sends a liaison
familyDesc.membership: Is part of, or takes part in
